title: The Letters That Came Every Month

lines.dialogue: A creditor paid in his own handwriting stood at the edge of the veranda, ink-stained fingers tracing the edge of an empty envelope.
lines.stage_directions: The first of the month had passed. The boatman had not come.

lines.dialogue: The veranda.
Wan sat at the scribe-table, blotting sand scattered across the page.
lines.stage_directions: Phum repaired spectacles at the rail. Pom sat cross-legged, pen moving. Rangsri hummed into her lacquered box. Phra Kam counted breaths by the pond. The boatman stood at the steps.

segments.dialogue: ทำหายที่ไหน — where did you lose it?
segments.speaker: char_boatman
segments.stage_directions: The boatman turned to Wan, holding up a torn envelope corner, water-stained.

lines.dialogue: The officer asked me ทำหายที่ไหน — where did you lose it? — like I’d dropped a coin wrapped in brown paper.
lines.stage_directions: He handed over a damp bundle tied with twine.

lines.dialogue: Mae’s reply sat in my hand, its creases sharp.
lines.stage_directions: Wan did not look up.

segments.dialogue: สนใจแค่ว่า — only interested in whether the letter went.
segments.speaker: char_phum
segments.stage_directions: Phum looked up from his lens.

lines.dialogue: He’s only interested in the envelopes with money. สนใจแค่ว่า.
lines.stage_directions: His voice was low, even.

lines.dialogue: To my respected mother, the third of the month approaches. Your dutiful son awaits your reply.
lines.stage_directions: He recited it softly, as if proofreading.

line.dialogue: The officer has the outgoing sack. Mae writes she hasn’t received. She asks why. What do we say?
line.stage_directions: Lek places the letter on the scribe-table. All turn to Wan, who stands at the scribe-table, blotting sand in hand.

choices.description: Write the apology letter to keep the remittance going as scheduled.

line.dialogue: I wrote the lines. Wan checked the date, the salutation, the amount.
line.stage_directions: He handed me four satang for the page.

line.dialogue: I hesitated. Wan turned the page over, blank side up.
line.stage_directions: The pen lay idle.

choices.description: Refuse to write the letter and let Wan face the delay directly.

line.dialogue: I said the letter must go with the sack. Wan’s hand tightened on the sand jar.
line.stage_directions: He did not speak.

line.dialogue: I opened my mouth, then closed it. Wan poured fresh sand.
line.stage_directions: The jar rattled like bones.

choices.description: Send the boatman back to the lock with a sealed apology.

line.dialogue: I paid the boatman extra. He took the envelope without a word.
line.stage_directions: The boat groaned as it turned.

line.dialogue: I offered the fare. The boatman shook his head.
line.stage_directions: He stepped back onto the dock.

lines.dialogue: The canal's broker of other sons' devotion walked the steps to the landing, inkstone in hand.
lines.stage_directions: Lek, Wan, Phum, the boatman, Pom, and Rangsri moved down the path. The landing waited, silent.

lines.dialogue: The pigeonhole rack held no new envelopes. The old women sat on the reading bench, silent.
lines.stage_directions: The air smelled of damp paper and waiting. A single brass weight sat in the rack's center slot — 15 baht, pledged.

lines.dialogue: The boatman’s boat was tied at the steps, empty.
lines.stage_directions: No sack had come down from the lock.

segments.dialogue: คุณจะเสียใจ — you'll regret it.
segments.speaker: char_phum
segments.stage_directions: He looked at Wan, then at the lock.

lines.dialogue: Push him, and you’ll regret it. คุณจะเสียใจ.
lines.stage_directions: Phum adjusted his lens, voice low.

lines.dialogue: To my respected mother, your dutiful son writes: the waters are high. The boat delayed.
lines.stage_directions: Wan dictated to no one, pen poised over scrap paper.

segments.dialogue: ขอบคุณที่เป็นห่วง — thanks for worrying.
segments.speaker: char_sangwan
segments.stage_directions: He said it flatly, not looking up.

lines.dialogue: ขอบคุณที่เป็นห่วง. But the letter must go.
lines.stage_directions: He did not look up.

lines.dialogue: Delay sits heavier than debt.
lines.stage_directions: Pom stood at the back, steel pen in hand, not writing.

lines.dialogue: The box hums for a laugh that hasn’t come.
lines.stage_directions: She placed a vial labeled *A joke not repeated* on the table.

line.dialogue: The officer has the sack. The letter is evidence. We cannot send another. What do we do?
line.stage_directions: Wan’s fingers tapped the inkstone — three taps, like a due date.

choices.description: Write a second letter to send when the sack is released.

line.dialogue: I wrote the second letter. Wan checked the paper's heft. Wan slipped the bracelet from his coat and turned toward the pawnshop.
line.stage_directions: He folded it precisely, creasing each edge twice.

line.dialogue: I reached for the pen. Wan covered the paper with his hand.
line.stage_directions: The inkstone remained closed.

choices.description: Confront the officer at the lock and demand the mail sack back.

line.dialogue: I walked to the lock. The officer returned the sack, smirking. Wan slipped the bracelet from his coat and turned toward the pawnshop.
line.stage_directions: The seal was broken.

line.dialogue: I opened my mouth. The officer turned his back.
line.stage_directions: The boatman untied his line.

choices.description: Go to the pawnshop to raise funds for a new delivery.

line.dialogue: I followed Wan down the path. The pawnshop bell chimed.
line.stage_directions: The party moved toward the canal market.

line.dialogue: I suggested the pawnshop. Wan did not move.
line.stage_directions: The inkstone stayed closed.

lines.dialogue: The gold bracelet entered the pawnshop on the twenty-eighth, pledged for 15 baht.
lines.stage_directions: Wan placed the bracelet on the glass. The appraiser did not look up.

lines.dialogue: The pawnshop.
Lek, Wan, Phum, the boatman, Pom, and Rangsri stood at the counter.
lines.stage_directions: The appraiser lifted the bracelet with brass tongs.

segments.dialogue: นั่นไง — there it is!
segments.speaker: char_pawnshop_appraiser
segments.stage_directions: He pointed to the ledger entry: '28th — bracelet, 15 baht. 3rd — redeemed.'

lines.dialogue: นั่นไง — there it is. Same as every month.
lines.stage_directions: He spoke to the gold on the scales.

lines.dialogue: To my respected mother, your dutiful son writes: the debt is due. The gold returns.
lines.stage_directions: Wan’s voice was precise, like pricing a page.

segments.dialogue: เขาวางสายไปแล้ว — he hung up.
segments.speaker: char_phum
segments.stage_directions: Phum murmured it, lens on the appraiser’s hands.

lines.dialogue: The district speaking-tube just went silent. เขาวางสายไปแล้ว — he hung up.
lines.stage_directions: He did not look up.

lines.dialogue: Gold weighs the same whether pledged or paid.
lines.stage_directions: Pom watched, pen still.

lines.dialogue: The box hums for a sound that hasn’t come.
lines.stage_directions: She placed a vial labeled *The first sip after fasting* on the counter.

line.dialogue: The appraiser offers 15 baht. The officer holds the letter. We can bribe, wait, or redeem early. What do we do?
line.stage_directions: Wan’s fingers tapped the counter — three taps, like a due date.

choices.description: Accept the 15 baht and bribe the officer to release the letter.

line.dialogue: I took the note. The gold vanished into the drawer.
line.stage_directions: Wan did not look at the bracelet.

line.dialogue: I reached for the note. The appraiser closed the drawer.
line.stage_directions: The scale remained on the counter.

choices.description: Wait until the third to redeem the bracelet and send a new letter.

line.dialogue: I closed the ledger. 'We wait,' I said.
line.stage_directions: Wan nodded once, then left without a word.

line.dialogue: I suggested waiting. Wan’s hand trembled on the door.
line.stage_directions: He did not leave.

choices.description: Redeem the bracelet now and send the money through the boatman.

line.dialogue: I paid the interest. The appraiser slid the bracelet back.
line.stage_directions: Wan placed it in his coat, not on his wrist.

line.dialogue: I counted the baht. The appraiser shook his head.
line.stage_directions: The drawer stayed closed.

lines.dialogue: The letters that came every month were no longer due, and Wan stood at the rail, coat buttoned tight.
lines.stage_directions: The party had returned to the veranda. Wan, Lek, Phum, Pom, Rangsri, Phra Kam, Kamnan Noi, and the boatman were present.

lines.dialogue: To my respected mother, your dutiful son writes: the boat comes. The gold is spent. The debt remains.
lines.stage_directions: Wan spoke to the water. No envelope. No pen.

lines.dialogue: The sun struck the water.
lines.stage_directions: No one moved toward the steps.

segments.dialogue: เข้ามาเลย — come in.
segments.speaker: char_pricha
segments.stage_directions: Lek spoke to the empty air where the boat would dock.

lines.dialogue: เข้ามาเลย. There’s tea.
lines.stage_directions: He stepped to the rail.

lines.dialogue: The pond holds what is given. It does not ask for return.
lines.stage_directions: He placed a grain of rice in the water. It sank.

lines.dialogue: The unsaid lines grow heavier with time.
lines.stage_directions: He added a mirror shard to his ledger.

segments.dialogue: น่าสนใจดีนะ — that's interesting.
segments.speaker: char_mor_duang
segments.stage_directions: Kamnan Noi stepped onto the veranda, chronometer in hand.

lines.dialogue: The hour of her coming matches the king’s last breath. น่าสนใจดีนะ.
lines.stage_directions: He adjusted his compass to the sun’s angle.

lines.dialogue: To the stars, to the water, to the unclaimed hand: your dutiful son writes. The third of the month comes. The gold returns. The letter goes.
lines.stage_directions: He spoke to the horizon. No one answered.

line.dialogue: She is coming. The letter is gone. The gold is spent. What do we do?
line.stage_directions: Wan stood at the rail, coat buttoned tight.

choices.description: Prepare the house with food and a place for her to rest.

line.dialogue: I laid out the mat. The kettle sang by noon.
line.stage_directions: Wan stood at the door, watching the bend.

line.dialogue: I fetched the mat. It remained rolled.
line.stage_directions: The kettle stayed cold.

choices.description: Meet her boat at the bend before she reaches the landing.

line.dialogue: I walked to the bend. She saw me and slowed the oar.
line.stage_directions: Wan followed, ten paces behind.

line.dialogue: I started down the path. My feet would not carry me.
line.stage_directions: The boat rounded the bend alone.

choices.description: Let Wan meet her alone, with no one else present.

line.dialogue: I turned away. 'This is not for us,' I said.
line.stage_directions: Wan walked to the steps. The boat touched wood.

line.dialogue: I hesitated at the rail. The boat was close.
line.stage_directions: Wan turned and said, 'Go back.'
